So it would appear that there are two main causes to this strange voting situation:

  1. The algorithm for ranking puts a greater emphasis on how quickly a post gets votes, vs the number of votes

  2. New voaters don't realize that their upvotes are potentially limited, and so spend them on the more clickbaity types of posts on the front page.

I like how the algorithm gives posts that wouldn't have had a chance on reddit a shot at the front page, but I think an improvement could be made in the communication of the rules to newcomers. When I first started it was very confusing to me as well, because I tried downvoting something, and it just didn't work. The popup message also didn't include any information about upvote limits. Having clearer communication about the upvote and downvote limitations would be nice.

This is what I would say:

  • If a bolt isn't threading in easily, it's probably crossthreaded. Always double check.

  • Especially if you're putting in a crank extractor

  • Don't buy cheap tools, they wear out faster

  • Do not invest money in any bike marked Magna, Huffy, Roadmaster, Free Spirit, or Ross.

  • If you see a puddle on the street, assume it's a deep pothole filled with urine

  • On long rides, eat before you feel hungry

  • Know your limits before riding under the influence of alcohol, if you can't walk than you sure as hell cannot pilot a bicycle

  • If the seal on your minipump is wearing out, replace it before going on any long rides.

  • Always carry basic tools, patch kit, and at least spare tube, no matter how short of a ride you plan to go on

  • Being a lone wolf cyclist is great, but you will grow much faster if you ride other people on occasion

  • Stick with Shimano

  • Don't buy jerseys without full zipper they're a pain in the ass to get off when you're sweaty and tired.

  • You know what's better than replacing flats on the side of the road before work? Just fucking buying gatorskins.

When I was a young boy I had a dog, Gojo. Insert typical boy and his dog story for a few years. One day, Gojo was sick, so we put him in a carrier, and drove him to the local vet. The vet said a bunch of technical vet things I didn't understand, then said he would have to be put to sleep and gave me a look. He suggested to my father that I be taken to the waiting room, but my innocent young mind assumed "put to sleep" meant litterally, put to sleep, so I insisted on staying. I watched Gojo "go to sleep", my father then paid the vet, and we left. On the ride home, I asked when Gojo would be better, and when we would go back to get him, and my father told me the saddest fucking thing I've ever been told in my life.

"You'll never see your dog again."

I have never had another dog.
